issues: Whether the Refugee Appeal Division's implausibility findings meet the standard that such findings be made only in the clearest of cases
Whether the Board reasonably relied on general country-condition documentation to reject an individualized account of attempted forced recruitment

Whether discounting a single expert source's reference to 'anecdotal evidence' of forced recruitment, and distinguishing urban from rural incidence, was reasonable given the claimant's specific circumstances

Whether the Board's finding that supporting documents (medical report, leases, family letters) failed to corroborate the recruitment allegation was reasonable given what those documents could realistically show

Whether the Board's reasoning was internally inconsistent or illogical in finding it implausible both that the group could not locate the claimant for two years and that armed men would abandon an abduction attempt when confronted
What weight, if any, recent Federal Court decisions addressing the same country documentation and similar recruitment allegations should have on judicial review of this decision
What standard of review (reasonableness) applies to the Refugee Appeal Division's plausibility and credibility findings on judicial review
key_facts: Claimant holds dual citizenship in two Middle Eastern countries and fled the one where he was residing
An armed political-militia group pressured him by phone for about two years to join fighters in a neighbouring country's war, escalating from appeals/money offers to threats
Claimant repeatedly changed phone number, job and address in the capital to evade the group
Masked men with machine guns forced entry into his mother's home and tried to drag him out, injuring his mother when she and his sister resisted; the men left empty-handed
The Refugee Appeal Division rejected the claim as implausible
The RAD relied on national documentation package material from academics, embassy staff and NGOs stating the group does not forcibly recruit
The RAD discounted a single expert's reference to anecdotal evidence of forced recruitment as occurring mainly in rural areas, distinguishing the claimant's urban residence
The RAD found it implausible that a group with claimed intelligence/military capacity could not locate the claimant for two years yet abandoned an armed abduction attempt when confronted by two women
The RAD found supporting evidence (medical report, leases, family letters) did not corroborate the recruitment allegation
Two recent Federal Court decisions involving the same country documentation and similar recruitment allegations found the Board's reasoning unreasonable
causes_of_action: Application for judicial review of a Refugee Appeal Division decision
